task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about the captioning work on Ternlight Theater's four-town tour and the choices involved in making a live performance accessible away from a permanent stage.

facts.text: A July 2026 rehearsal note records caption operator Ceri Varden marking a changed pause in the script before Ternlight Theater's next tour performance.
The company toured the original fictional play Four Rooms for Rain to four town halls rather than a permanent theater.
Caption text was prepared from the approved script and advanced by a trained operator following the live performance.
The system was not described as an automatic guarantee that every unscripted line would immediately appear correctly.
The tour's approved $9,000 captioning budget allocated $3,000 to reusable display equipment, $4,000 to text preparation and $2,000 to operator time; final expenditure is not supplied.
The equipment can be reused, but later productions still require preparation, rehearsal and operator work.
The four performances recorded attendances of 80, 100, 60 and 120, totaling 360 admissions.
The admissions include repeat theatergoers and do not establish the number who attended specifically because captions were available.
Each hall required a separate check of screen position, stage sightlines and cable routes.
A front-row position that gave a clear stage view at one hall made the captions difficult to follow at another, according to the access rehearsal notes.
Deaf audience member Neri Calven attended one performance after asking where the caption display would be placed.
Calven's supplied written comment was, "Being told captions exist is the first answer. Being able to see them and the actors is the next one."
Varden said, "The text is prepared, but the timing still belongs to the people performing it tonight."
The company built caption preparation into paid production work rather than asking local volunteers to transcribe each show on arrival.
A grant was awarded to cover this tour's captioning budget; funding for future tours has not been secured.
Director Omi Braven says portable equipment broadens venue options but adds transport and setup tasks.
The record contains no controlled attendance or revenue comparison proving the captions paid for themselves.
Captioning does not by itself provide step-free entry, audio description or every other access service a hall might need.
Ternlight normally travels with sets designed to fit in one small truck, and the displays shared that transport.
The company is collecting venue-specific feedback rather than declaring a single screen arrangement suitable everywhere.

forbidden_additions: Automatic perfect transcription, 360 new caption users or a proved revenue gain
The grant funds every future tour or captions solve all venue-access needs
